citation: Czermak P, Amman F, Jantsch MF, Cimatti L. Organ-wide profiling in mouse reveals high editing levels of Filamin B mRNA in the musculoskeletal system. RNA Biology. 2018. doi:10.1080/15476286.2018.1480252.
description: This mouse tissue survey identified ADAR2 as the enzyme responsible for Filamin B RNA editing and documented regulated FLNB editing across organs and postnatal development. It supports a specific ADARB1-to-Flnb bridge, but it measures editing of Flnb rather than predicting loss of Flnb transcript abundance.

citation: Jain M, Weber A, Maly K, Manjaly G, Deek J, Tsvyetkova O, Stulic M, Toca-Herrera JL, Jantsch MF. A-to-I RNA editing of Filamin A regulates cellular adhesion, migration and mechanical properties. FEBS Journal. 2022. doi:10.1111/febs.16391.
description: This study showed that ADAR2-mediated editing of Flna changes actin crosslinking, cellular stiffness, adhesion, and migration. It provides a specific ADARB1-to-filamin cytoskeletal bridge without establishing a direction for Flna or Flnb mRNA abundance after ADARB1 loss.

citation: Malek N, Mrowczynska E, Michrowska A, Mazurkiewicz E, Pavlyk I, Mazur AJ. Knockout of ACTB and ACTG1 with CRISPR/Cas9(D10A) Technique Shows that Non-Muscle beta and gamma Actin Are Not Equal in Relation to Human Melanoma Cells' Motility and Focal Adhesion Formation. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2020. doi:10.3390/ijms21082746.
description: Human ACTB or ACTG1 knockout clones showed reciprocal compensation by the remaining non-muscle actin isoform and altered focal-adhesion behavior. This is a target-specific precedent for ACTB loss increasing Actg1-like compensation, but it does not directly predict Flna transcription in neurons.

citation: Knoedler JR, Avila-Mendoza J, Subramani A, Denver RJ. The Paralogous Kruppel-like Factors 9 and 13 Regulate the Mammalian Cellular Circadian Clock Output Gene Dbp. Journal of Biological Rhythms. 2020. doi:10.1177/0748730420913205.
description: This work places Dbp, Tef, Per genes, Nr1d1, and Nr1d2 within the mammalian CLOCK/BMAL1 transcriptional feedback-loop neighborhood and experimentally uses CLOCK/BMAL1-dependent activation of a Dbp reporter. It supports the expectation that Clock loss reduces clock-output transcripts such as Dbp, Tef, Per3, and Nr1d2.

citation: Miserez AR, Muller PY, Barella L, Barella S, Staehelin HB, Leitersdorf E, Kark JD, Friedlander Y. Sterol-regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP)-2 contributes to polygenic hypercholesterolaemia. Atherosclerosis. 2002. doi:10.1016/s0021-9150(01)00762-6.
description: The paper describes activated SREBP-2 as a transcriptional activator of cholesterol homeostasis genes, including LDL receptor, HMG-CoA synthase, and HMG-CoA reductase. It directly supports the prediction that Srebf2 loss decreases a sterol-biosynthesis and uptake module.

citation: Sharpe LJ, Brown AJ. Rapamycin down-regulates LDL-receptor expression independently of SREBP-2. Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications. 2008. doi:10.1016/j.bbrc.2008.06.108.
description: This study states and tests the canonical role of SREBP-2 in up-regulating genes for cholesterol synthesis and uptake, including HMG-CoA reductase and LDL receptor. It supplies direct target-to-module support for reduced cholesterol-pathway transcripts after Srebf2 loss.

citation: Bar-Peled L, Chantranupong L, Cherniack AD, Chen WW, Ottina KA, Grabiner BC, Spear ED, Carter SL, Meyerson M, Sabatini DM. A tumor suppressor complex with GAP activity for the Rag GTPases that signal amino acid sufficiency to mTORC1. Science. 2013. doi:10.1126/science.1232044.
description: This paper identified GATOR1 as a DEPDC5-NPRL2-NPRL3 GAP complex that inhibits Rag-dependent mTORC1 activation under amino-acid starvation. It supports the first step of the DEPDC5 loss to mTORC1 activation bridge.

citation: Li H, Min Q, Ouyang C, Lee J, He C, Zou MH, Xie Z. AMPK activation prevents excess nutrient-induced hepatic lipid accumulation by inhibiting mTORC1 signaling and endoplasmic reticulum stress response. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta. 2014. doi:10.1016/j.bbadis.2014.07.002.
description: This study connected mTORC1 activation, including activation produced by Tsc2 deletion, to an SREBP-1 and endoplasmic-reticulum-stress lipid-accumulation program. It provides a specific but indirect bridge from TSC2 or DEPDC5 loss to lipid-regulatory transcripts, leaving the neuronal SREBP2/LDLR direction incompletely determined.
